content: 1. Long-acting buprenorphine injections administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors require close monitoring to ensure adequate plasma levels of buprenorphine. If signs of toxicity or overdose occur within two weeks and the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, transition the patient to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. 2. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases buspirone levels through the same mechanism. A reduced dose of buspirone may be required, and close monitoring is recommended. 3. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Darunavir increases cabazitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may increase toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Darunavir increases cabergoline levels by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Cobicistat increases cabozantinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If necessary, reduce the cabozantinib dose (40 mg/day for Cometriq or 20 mg/day for Cabometyx) and resume the previous dose 2-3 days after discontinuing the inhibitor. 7. Darunavir increases calcifediol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially altering vitamin D metabolism. Monitor serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium levels closely when initiating or discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 8. Darunavir increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose and monitor closely. 9. Darunavir increases capivasertib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 10. Darunavir increases capmatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Carbamazepine decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Darunavir increases cariprazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of cariprazine is required when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 13. Darunavir increases carvedilol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Cenobamate decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of darunavir as needed and monitor closely. 15. Darunavir increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the ceritinib dose by approximately 33% if unavoidable. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 16. Darunavir increases cevimeline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Chloramphenicol increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Darunavir increases chlordiazepoxide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for increased toxicity and consider alternatives if available. 19. Darunavir increases ciclesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for increased toxicity. 20. Darunavir increases cilostazol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the cilostazol dose to 50 mg twice daily and monitor for adverse effects. 21. Cimetidine increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Darunavir increases cinacalcet levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Cobicistat increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose titration of antidepressants may be required. 24. Darunavir increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider alternative antibiotics if coadministered with darunavir. Monitor closely. 25. Cobicistat increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose and monitor for response. 26. Darunavir increases clonazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Darunavir decreases clopidogrel activation by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced efficacy. 28. Cobicistat increases clorazepate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose if necessary and monitor closely. 29. Darunavir increases clozapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Cobicistat increases cobimetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 31. Cobicistat increases colchicine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid colchicine use in patients with renal or hepatic impairment due to the risk of serious reactions. Adjust the colchicine dose if necessary. 32. Cobicistat increases conivaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 33. Darunavir decreases conjugated estrogens' effects through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Darunavir increases copanlisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
